en: Thick Wheat Noodles
Thick wheat noodles kept warm under a cheap heat lamp, going a little softer with every hour of the shift.
Soy Broth
Stock simmered down overnight until it coats the back of a spoon, dark and salt-heavy.
Citrus Chili Paste
Fermented chilies pounded down with citrus peel, sharp enough to catch the back of the throat.
Solar Rig Tech
Something hearty and savory, please — I've been rewiring solar panels on the north tower all shift and I want to feel human again.
Hearty and savory. Wants to feel human again.
Warm, filling, exactly what these hands needed.
Good and warm — hit the spot after a shift like this.
Decent, but it's not quite the hearty plate I was hoping for.
This isn't going to cut it after the shift I've had.
Scrap-Market Trader
Something comforting with just a little kick — but keep the soy out, or I'll be miserable by morning.
Comforting, just a little kick. No soy.
Good warmth, no surprises — my stomach's still on my side.
Good warmth, good kick, and my stomach's still on my side.
It's alright, but it's not really what I asked for.
This isn't it. My stomach and I are going to have words about this one.
No soy, whatever you do — my stomach's been fighting it for years.
Rooftop Lettuce
Lettuce pulled straight from the truck's rooftop planter — crisp, cool, and the closest thing to fresh air on this block.
Late-Shift Medic
Something fresh and light, please — nothing heavy. I've been elbow-deep in triage since second shift and my stomach won't forgive anything rich right now.
Fresh and light. Nothing heavy or rich.
Light, clean, and exactly what my stomach needed after a shift like that.
Good and light. First thing all shift that hasn't sat like a stone.
It's alright, but heavier than I wanted after tonight.
This is way too heavy. My stomach's not going to forgive either of us for this.
Mushrooms
Wild mushrooms, sliced thick, sweated down slow until they give up their own dark liquid.
Chili Crisp
Dried chilies and shallots fried down in oil until they turn brittle, spooned out still warm from the pan.
Kimchi
Napa cabbage packed in chili paste and left to sour in a sealed jar until the lid won't stay quiet.
Smoked Fish
Fillets cured in salt, then hung over smoldering wood chips until the flesh turns a deep, glossy amber.
Coconut Milk
Coconut flesh grated, soaked, and squeezed through cloth until the liquid runs rich and pale, thick enough to slow a boil.
Pickled Cucumber
Cucumbers sliced thin and packed in vinegar brine until they turn translucent and snap clean in half.
Chickpeas
Dried chickpeas soaked overnight, then simmered slow until they soften enough to mash between two fingers.
Citrus Herbs
A fistful of soft herbs torn over citrus zest, bruised just enough to let the oils out.
Rig Partner
We've been up on the north tower together since sunup, and the heat up there doesn't let up — give me something crisp and fresh, and don't be shy putting real spice on it. I want to feel it.
Crisp and fresh — and real spice, not shy.
Now that's worth climbing back up for. Save the recipe — my partner's going to want to know.
Solid. This'll carry both of us through the rest of the shift.
It's alright. Was hoping for something with a bit more to it, honestly.
My partner's going to laugh when I hear what I paid for this.
Office Worker

Compliance ran out of the good trays hours ago and I still needed lunch. Give me something really fresh, and don't be afraid to get adventurous with it — anything but another sad sandwich from that conference room.
Really fresh, and adventurous with it.
This is exactly what that conference room lunch could never be. Worth the walk.
Better than anything on the catering cart. I might even make it back before the meeting starts.
It's a step up from the break room, at least.
I skipped a meeting for this? I should have just eaten the sad sandwich.
Night Courier

Route's got two more stops before the timer runs out. Make it comforting — really comforting — and give me actual spice this time, not just a hint. Just keep anything fermented off my plate; my stomach's already arguing with me tonight.
Really comforting, with actual spice. Nothing fermented.
Now that's fuel. I'm already thinking about the next drop.
That'll hold me to the last stop. Good call.
It'll do. Was hoping it'd hit harder, though.
This isn't getting me through the rest of the route.
Nothing sour or fermented tonight — my stomach's already arguing with me on this route.
Block Boss

This corner's mine, so for once I get to sit and actually eat instead of just watching it. Make it savory, and put some real heat on it while you're at it — but skip anything smoked. I don't trust anything that hides what's underneath it.
Savory with real heat. Nothing smoked.
Now this is why I let you park on my corner.
Not bad. You can stay another night.
It's fine. Don't get comfortable.
This corner's mine, and even I wouldn't serve this.
Skip anything smoked. Smoke's for hiding what's underneath, and I don't miss what's happening on my own corner.
Old Local

I've watched trucks come and go off this corner for years, and eaten off plenty of them. Keep it savory — hearty enough to matter — and don't try anything adventurous on me. And nothing that's been sitting under a heat lamp all shift; I can tell the difference. Just make it taste like something I'd actually recognize.
Savory and hearty. Nothing adventurous, nothing held under the lamp.
Now that's a plate. Tastes like something this block used to make, before everyone forgot how.
Good, honest food. Can't complain about that.
It's fine. I've had better off carts that don't exist anymore.
I've outlasted worse than you on this corner, and this still isn't it.
Nothing held under a heat lamp all shift. I've eaten off this corner long enough to tell what was made today from what's just been kept warm.
Staples
Broths and fats
Heat and ferment
Fresh and cured
